Larry, saw Daxko acquired Exercise.com to broaden its boutique fitness footprint, on top of a steady run of acquisitions.

Folding in new products and segments usually means more in-market accounts than the sales team can cover, and that is where good-fit deals quietly stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Daxko off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Larry, quick follow-up for Daxko.

After a string of acquisitions, the addressable market grows faster than your selling capacity can. Most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to book to cover the expanded base, so the gap shows up late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Daxko needs across the boutique and club segments this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Larry, last bit of proof for Daxko.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Daxko's reply rate likely compares to other vertical SaaS firms growing by acquisition. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?

If scaling pipeline across the new segments without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integrating fresh acquisitions is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a multi-segment SaaS motion? I will tailor it to Daxko either way.
